questions.query: What cybersecurity risks does Microsoft describe?
questions.reference_answer: Microsoft says cyberthreats are becoming more sophisticated and difficult to detect; security breaches can disrupt services, expose customer data, compromise intellectual property, enable ransomware, damage its reputation or competitive position, and increase remediation costs; supply-chain attacks can introduce malware through software updates; and product vulnerabilities can persist when customers have not installed security updates or attackers exploited the vulnerabilities before patches were available.

required_facts.claim: Cyberthreats are evolving, increasingly sophisticated, and harder to detect and defend against.

evidence_units.quote: Cyberthreats are constantly evolving and becoming increasingly sophisticated and complex, increasing the difficulty of detecting and successfully defending against them.

required_facts.claim: Security breaches can cause operational disruption, privacy harm, intellectual-property loss, ransomware exposure, reputational or competitive harm, remediation costs, and product development delays.

evidence_units.quote: Breaches of our facilities, network, or data security could disrupt the security of our systems and business applications, impair our ability to provide services to our customers and protect the privacy of their data, result in product development delays, compromise confidential or technical business information harming our reputation or competitive position, result in theft or misuse of our intellectual property or other assets, subject us to ransomware attacks, require us to allocate more resources to improve technologies or remediate the impacts of attacks, or otherwise adversely affect our business.

required_facts.claim: Supply-chain cyberattacks can introduce malware through a software provider's updates.

evidence_units.quote: We are also subject to supply chain cyberattacks where malware can be introduced to a software provider’s customers, including us, through software updates.

required_facts.claim: Product vulnerabilities can persist when customers do not install security updates or attackers exploit the vulnerabilities before patching.

evidence_units.quote: Vulnerabilities in these or any product can persist even after we have issued security patches if customers have not installed the most recent updates, or if the attackers exploited the vulnerabilities before patching to install additional malware to further compromise customers’ systems.

optional_facts.claim: Stolen account information and inadequate account-security practices can enable account compromise, unauthorized access, ransomware, or other malicious software.

evidence_units.quote: Adversaries that acquire user account information can use that information to compromise our users’ accounts, including where accounts share the same attributes such as passwords. Inadequate account security practices may also result in unauthorized access, and user activity may result in ransomware or other malicious software impacting a customer’s use of our products or services.

optional_facts.claim: Vulnerabilities in open-source software can make Microsoft's products susceptible to cyberattacks.

evidence_units.quote: There may be vulnerabilities in open source software that may make our products susceptible to cyberattacks.

optional_facts.claim: Generative-AI features may face unanticipated security threats while risks and protections are still developing.

evidence_units.quote: Because generative AI is a new field, understanding of security risks and protection methods continues to develop; features that rely on generative AI may be susceptible to unanticipated security threats from sophisticated adversaries.

optional_facts.claim: Outdated security standards and customers' limited technical capabilities can increase vulnerability to attacks.

evidence_units.quote:
Failure to utilize the most current security advances and standards can increase our customers’ vulnerability to attack. Further, customers of widely varied size and technical sophistication use our technology, and consequently may still
have limited capabilities and resources to help them adopt and implement state of the art cybersecurity practices and technologies.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft may be unable to detect or track attacks in customer environments where it has limited visibility, particularly on-premises systems.

evidence_units.quote: We may not be able to detect the existence or extent of these attacks for all of our customers or have information on how to detect or track an attack, especially where an attack involves on-premises software such as Exchange Server where we may have no or limited visibility into our customers’ computing environments.

optional_facts.claim: Security investments can reduce operating margins, while inadequate defenses can harm Microsoft's reputation and delay customer purchases or adoption.

evidence_units.quote: The cost of measures to protect products and customer-facing services could reduce our operating margins. If we fail to do these things well, actual or perceived security vulnerabilities in our products and services, data corruption issues, or reduced performance could harm our reputation and lead customers to reduce or delay future purchases of products or subscriptions to services, or to use competing products or services. Customers may also spend more on protecting their existing computer systems from attack, which could delay adoption of additional products or services.

optional_facts.claim: Security vulnerabilities in third-party components can cause costs, liability, lost revenue, and reputational or competitive harm.

evidence_units.quote: Our products operate in conjunction with and are dependent on products and components across a broad ecosystem of third parties. If there is a security vulnerability in one of these components, and if there is a security exploit targeting it, we could face increased costs, liability claims, reduced revenue, or harm to our reputation or competitive position.

optional_facts.claim: Security controls may not prevent improper disclosure or misuse of personal data, creating reputational, legal, cost, and revenue risks.

evidence_units.quote: Despite our efforts to improve the security controls across our business groups and geographies, it is possible our security controls over personal data, our training of employees and third parties on data security, and other practices we follow may not prevent the improper disclosure or misuse of customer or user data we or our vendors store and manage. In addition, third parties who have limited access to our customer or user data may use this data in unauthorized ways. Improper disclosure or misuse could harm our reputation, lead to legal exposure to customers or users, or subject us to liability under laws that protect personal data, resulting in increased costs or loss of revenue.

optional_facts.claim: Perceptions that personal information is inadequately protected can inhibit sales and cloud adoption.

evidence_units.quote: Despite our efforts to protect customer and user data, perceptions that the collection, use, and retention of personal information is not satisfactorily protected could inhibit sales of our products or services and could limit adoption of our cloud-based solutions by consumers, businesses, and government entities.

questions.query: What risks does Microsoft describe related to AI?
questions.reference_answer: Microsoft says AI algorithms or training methods may be flawed, datasets may be insufficient or biased, and generated content may be offensive, illegal, or harmful. Inadequate AI development or deployment can impair adoption, cause products to malfunction, or harm individuals, customers, or society, and some outputs may require human review. Microsoft also faces competitive harm, regulatory action, legal liability under data-protection, privacy, intellectual-property, and other laws, and brand or reputational harm. Ethical issues, unintended uses, and effects on human rights, privacy, employment, or other societal matters can further harm its reputation, business, and financial results.

required_facts.claim: AI algorithms or training methods may be flawed, datasets may be overbroad, insufficient, or biased, and generated content may be offensive, illegal, or harmful.

evidence_units.quote: AI algorithms or training methodologies may be flawed. Datasets may be overbroad, insufficient, or contain biased information. Content generated by AI systems may be offensive, illegal, or otherwise harmful.

required_facts.claim: Inadequate AI development or deployment can impair adoption, cause products or services to malfunction, harm individuals, customers, or society, and require human review of some outputs.

evidence_units.quote: Ineffective or inadequate AI development or deployment practices by Microsoft or others could result in incidents that impair the acceptance of AI solutions or cause harm to individuals, customers, or society, or result in our products and services not working as intended. Human review of certain outputs may be required.

required_facts.claim: Implementing AI may expose Microsoft to competitive harm, regulatory action, legal liability under data-protection, privacy, intellectual-property, and other laws, and brand or reputational harm.

evidence_units.quote: As a result of these and other challenges associated with innovative technologies, our implementation of AI systems could subject us to competitive harm, regulatory action, legal liability, including under new proposed legislation regulating AI in jurisdictions such as the European Union (“EU”), new applications of existing data protection, privacy, intellectual property, and other laws, and brand or reputational harm.

required_facts.claim: Ethical issues, unintended consequences or uses, and controversial effects on human rights, privacy, employment, or other societal matters may harm Microsoft's reputation, business, and financial results.

evidence_units.quote: Some AI scenarios present ethical issues or may have broad impacts on society. If we enable or offer AI solutions that have unintended consequences, unintended usage or customization by our customers and partners, or are controversial because of their impact on human rights, privacy, employment, or other social, economic, or political issues, we may experience brand or reputational harm, adversely affecting our business and consolidated financial statements.

optional_facts.claim: AI is a highly competitive and rapidly changing market that requires substantial development and operating costs and responsiveness to technology, regulation, and public scrutiny.

evidence_units.quote: We expect AI technology and services to be a highly competitive and rapidly evolving market. We will bear significant development and operational costs to build and support the AI capabilities, products, and services necessary to meet the needs of our customers. To compete effectively we must also be responsive to technological change, potential regulatory developments, and public scrutiny.

optional_facts.claim: Using generative AI in Microsoft's internal systems may create new attack methods for adversaries.

evidence_units.quote: Increasing use of generative AI models in our internal systems may create new attack methods for adversaries.

optional_facts.claim: Regulatory constraints on using data for AI services may prevent Microsoft from realizing expected investment returns.

evidence_units.quote: Our investment in gaining insights from data is becoming central to the value of the services, including AI services, we deliver to customers, to operational efficiency and key opportunities in monetization, and to customer perceptions of quality. Our ability to use data in this way may be constrained by regulatory developments that impede realizing the expected return from this investment.

optional_facts.claim: Emerging AI regulation may increase costs or reduce opportunities for Microsoft's AI services.

evidence_units.quote: Legislative and regulatory action is emerging in the areas of AI and content moderation, which could increase costs or restrict opportunity. For example, in the EU, an AI Act is being considered, and may entail increased costs or decreased opportunities for the operation of our AI services in the European market.

questions.query: How does Microsoft describe competition in its business?
questions.reference_answer: Microsoft describes competition across its major product families. Office competes with global software, web, mobile, and local application providers; LinkedIn competes across professional networking, recruiting, advertising, sales intelligence, and learning, while Dynamics competes with cloud and on-premises business applications. Azure competes with major cloud vendors and open-source offerings, and server products face many operating-system and application alternatives. Windows competes with alternative software platforms and devices, particularly Apple and Google. Xbox and cloud gaming compete with gaming ecosystems, streaming and entertainment services, and Nintendo and Sony consoles, while search and news advertising competes with Google, Meta, websites, and online portals.

required_facts.claim: Office competes with global software and application vendors as well as web, mobile, and local application providers.

evidence_units.quote: Competitors to Office include software and global application vendors, such as Apple, Cisco Systems, Meta, Google, Okta, Proofpoint, Slack, Symantec, Zoom, and numerous web-based and mobile application competitors as well as local application developers.

required_facts.claim: LinkedIn competes in professional networking, recruiting, talent management, advertising, sales intelligence, and learning, while Dynamics competes with cloud and on-premises business-solution providers.

evidence_units.quote:
LinkedIn faces competition from online professional networks, recruiting companies, talent management companies, and larger companies that are focusing on talent management and human resource services; job boards; traditional recruiting firms; and companies that provide learning and development products and services. Marketing Solutions competes with online and offline outlets that generate revenue from advertisers and marketers, and Sales Solutions competes with online and offline outlets for companies with lead generation and customer intelligence and insights.
Dynamics competes with cloud-based and on-premises business solution providers such as Oracle, Salesforce, and SAP.

required_facts.claim: Azure competes with major cloud vendors and open-source offerings, and Microsoft differentiates it through hybrid-cloud integration and scale.

evidence_units.quote: Azure faces diverse competition from companies such as Amazon, Google, IBM, Oracle, VMware, and open source offerings. Azure’s competitive advantage includes enabling a hybrid cloud, allowing deployment of existing datacenters with our public cloud into a single, cohesive infrastructure, and the ability to run at a scale that meets the needs of businesses of all sizes and complexities.

required_facts.claim: Microsoft's server products face broad competition from server operating systems and applications offered through varied market approaches.

evidence_units.quote: Our server products face competition from a wide variety of server operating systems and applications offered by companies with a range of market approaches.

required_facts.claim: Windows competes with alternative software products, platforms, and devices, especially those from Apple and Google.

evidence_units.quote: Windows faces competition from various software products and from alternative platforms and devices, mainly from Apple and Google.

required_facts.claim: Xbox and cloud gaming compete with gaming ecosystems, game and video streaming services, and established Nintendo and Sony console platforms.

evidence_units.quote: Xbox and our cloud gaming services face competition from various online gaming ecosystems and game streaming services, including those operated by Amazon, Apple, Meta, and Tencent. We also compete with other providers of entertainment services such as video streaming platforms. Our gaming platform competes with console platforms from Nintendo and Sony, both of which have a large, established base of customers.

required_facts.claim: Microsoft's search and news advertising business competes with Google, Meta, websites, and online portals.

evidence_units.quote: Our Search and news advertising business competes with Google and a wide array of websites, social platforms like Meta, and portals that provide content and online offerings to end users.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft differentiates its productivity tools through power, flexibility, security, integration, ease of use, industry specificity, and compatibility with existing on-premises and cloud technology.

evidence_units.quote: We compete by providing powerful, flexible, secure, integrated industry-specific, and easy-to-use productivity and collaboration tools and services that create comprehensive solutions and work well with technologies our customers already have both on-premises or in the cloud.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft's AI offerings compete with hyperscalers, emerging companies, partners, and open-source solutions.

evidence_units.quote: Our AI offerings compete with AI products from hyperscalers such as Amazon Bedrock, Amazon CodeWhisperer, and Google AI, as well as products from other emerging competitors, many of which are also current or potential partners, including Meta’s LLaMA2 and other open source solutions.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft competes with commercial software vendors across enterprise platforms, connectivity, security, hosting, databases, and e-business servers.

evidence_units.quote: We compete to provide enterprise-wide computing solutions and point solutions with numerous commercial software vendors that offer solutions and middleware technology platforms, software applications for connectivity (both Internet and intranet), security, hosting, database, and e-business servers.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft differentiates server products through performance, ownership costs, productivity, applications, development tools, compatibility, security, and manageability.

evidence_units.quote: We believe our server products provide customers with advantages in performance, total costs of ownership, and productivity by delivering superior applications, development tools, compatibility with a broad base of hardware and software applications, security, and manageability.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft devices compete with computer, tablet, and hardware manufacturers across design, technology, and price, including firms that are also partners or customers.

evidence_units.quote: Devices face competition from various computer, tablet, and hardware manufacturers who offer a unique combination of high-quality industrial design and innovative technologies across various price points. These manufacturers, many of which are also current or potential partners and customers, include Apple and our Windows OEMs.

optional_facts.claim: Microsoft differentiates gaming through hardware, interfaces, developer tools, online services, and exclusive first-party and digital content.

evidence_units.quote: We believe our gaming platform is effectively positioned against, and uniquely differentiated from, competitive products and services based on significant innovation in hardware architecture, user interface, developer tools, online gaming and entertainment services, and continued strong exclusive content from our own first-party game franchises as well as other digital content offerings.
